source: 05-MIGRATION.md C4 — the dependency audit gate. Read by web/scripts/audit-gate.mjs.
policy: An exception may only ever cover a devDependency chain. The production audit (`npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev`) is gated at zero advisories and consults nothing in this file — an entry naming a package that the production tree also reaches is rejected by the script rather than honoured.

exceptions.justification: Two CWE-835 infinite-loop denial-of-service advisories in image-size's ICNS and JXL/HEIF parsers, both fixed in no published release (`fixAvailable: false` as of this date). The package is reached only from @storybook/nextjs-vite, a devDependency: it parses image files at Storybook build time so `next/image` can be mocked, and the only images it is ever handed are the ones in this repository. `npm audit --omit=dev` reports zero advisories, so nothing that ships to a browser or to the container reaches this code. Remove this entry the day @storybook/nextjs-vite ships a release whose vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs pulls a fixed image-size — the script fails on a stale entry, so it cannot be forgotten.

Not an advisory of its own: npm reports this package as high-severity purely because it depends on the image-size entry above, and it is listed separately because `npm audit` counts it separately (the reported total of three is three packages carrying two upstream GHSAs, not three distinct defects). Same dev-only reachability, same removal condition: it is a build-time Storybook framework plugin, absent from `npm audit --omit=dev` and from every shipped bundle.

The direct devDependency at the head of the same chain, reported high for the same two image-size advisories and for no defect of its own. WO-06 introduced it (04-ARCHITECTURE.md §5.2) and the C4 baseline of zero was captured before that, which is why the ruling recorded in the WO-24 PR body splits the gate: production dependencies stay at zero, and this dev chain is gated by name here instead of being waved through by a lowered --audit-level.

The direct devDependency at the head of this chain, added by WO-29 for the nightly Lighthouse gate (04-ARCHITECTURE.md §8.4, 05-MIGRATION.md C11). npm reports it high for the four advisories carried by its own transitive tree — `tmp` (two) via the `inquirer` prompt it never runs unattended, `uuid` (moderate, listed here because npm attributes it upward) and `extract-zip` via `lighthouse > puppeteer-core > @puppeteer/browsers` — and for no defect of its own. `fixAvailable` names `@lhci/cli@0.1.0`, a downgrade of five minor versions to a release that predates the assertion syntax this gate is written in, so there is nothing to upgrade to. Reachability: this package is executed only by `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` and by `npm run lhci` on a developer's machine, against a Compose stack on 127.0.0.1; it is absent from `npm audit --omit=dev`, from every shipped bundle and from web/Dockerfile's production stage. The two file-system advisories (`tmp`, `extract-zip`) need an attacker who can already write to the runner's temp directory or serve the Chrome download, at which point the runner is lost regardless. Remove this entry the day @lhci/cli ships a release whose tree pulls fixed `tmp` and `extract-zip` — the script fails on a stale entry, so it cannot be forgotten.

Not an advisory of its own: npm reports this package high purely because it depends on the same pinned `lighthouse`, and so on down to `extract-zip`. It is listed separately because `npm audit` counts packages, not defects — the seven WO-29 entries in this file are seven packages carrying four upstream GHSAs. Same dev-only reachability and the same removal condition as the `@lhci/cli` entry above.

Lighthouse itself, pinned by @lhci/cli to an exact version (12.6.1) — which is the point: the audit tool has to be a fixed version or the budgets in web/lighthouserc.json would be measured against a moving scoring curve. Reported high only for the `extract-zip` symlink advisory two levels below it, through `puppeteer-core > @puppeteer/browsers`. It has no advisory of its own, it runs only in the nightly workflow and on a developer's machine, and it is absent from `npm audit --omit=dev`.

Lighthouse's browser driver, reported high only for the `extract-zip` advisory one level below it. No defect of its own and no separate upgrade path: its version is fixed by the `lighthouse` pin above. Dev-only, absent from the production audit and from every shipped bundle.

The browser-download helper that owns the `extract-zip` dependency. Reported high for that one advisory and nothing else. It is not even exercised here: `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` resolves the runner's preinstalled google-chrome-stable into CHROME_PATH and `web/lighthouserc.json` drives that binary, so no archive is downloaded or unpacked by this tier at all. Dev-only, absent from the production audit.

The one real defect in this chain: `extract-zip` <= 2.0.1 follows symlinks out of the extraction directory, so an attacker who controls the archive can write outside it. Exploiting it needs a hostile Chrome archive, which needs control of the Puppeteer download host — and this tier downloads no archive at all, because the nightly points CHROME_PATH at the runner's preinstalled Chrome. `fixAvailable` names a @lhci/cli downgrade to 0.1.0 rather than a fixed extract-zip, so there is no version to move to. Dev-only, absent from `npm audit --omit=dev` and from the production image. Remove this entry when @puppeteer/browsers ships with extract-zip > 2.0.1 in the tree @lhci/cli resolves.

Two path-traversal advisories in `tmp` — an unsanitized `prefix`/`postfix` and a symlinked `dir` parameter — both requiring the caller to pass attacker-controlled options. @lhci/cli passes neither: it uses `tmp` for the scratch directory `lhci collect` writes LHRs into, with no user input on the path. The second copy in the tree is `external-editor`'s, reached only from `inquirer`'s interactive prompt, which the nightly never triggers because it runs `lhci autorun --config=<file>` with every answer already in the file. `fixAvailable` names a @lhci/cli downgrade to 0.1.0, not a fixed `tmp`. Dev-only, absent from the production audit and from the shipped image.
